lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Shape and Position
lesson.summary: Angles, polygons, symmetry and Islamic star patterns, coordinates, reflection, 3D shapes and nets.
learning_objectives: Find lines of symmetry and use coordinates

standards.text: Identify acute and obtuse angles; compare and classify shapes; lines of symmetry; describe positions on a 2-D grid

success_criteria: I can name acute, right and obtuse angles
I can find lines of symmetry
I can read coordinates and describe faces, edges and vertices
lesson.real_life: Tile patterns in mosques, reading maps, and buildings made from cubes, cylinders and pyramids.

blocks.alt: A black, orange and white butterfly with its wings open, showing symmetry
blocks.caption: A butterfly's two wings match, like a mirror image.
blocks.say: Welcome back, number explorer! Have you ever looked closely at the tiles on a mosque wall? They are made from stars, squares and triangles that fit together perfectly. Mathematicians and artists planned them with angles and symmetry. Today you will name angles and polygons. You will find lines of symmetry and plot points on a grid. You will also fold nets into 3D shapes. Let's go!

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do shapes fit together to make beautiful patterns and buildings?

blocks.alt: Mosque tiles use shapes and symmetry.
blocks.caption: Mosque tiles use shapes and symmetry.

blocks.markdown:
An **angle** is a turn. A **right angle** is 90°. **Acute** is smaller than 90°. **Obtuse** is bigger than 90° but smaller than 180°.

A straight line is 180°.
blocks.say: An angle is the amount of turn between two lines that meet at a point. We measure angles in degrees. Look at a clock. At three o'clock, the hands make a square corner. That is a right angle, exactly ninety degrees. An angle smaller than a right angle is acute. An angle bigger than a right angle, but smaller than a straight line, is obtuse. A straight line is one hundred and eighty degrees.

scenes.caption: Acute: 60°
scenes.say: At two o'clock the hands make a small, sharp angle. That is an acute angle, sixty degrees.

scenes.caption: Right angle: 90°
scenes.say: At three o'clock the hands make a square corner. That is a right angle, ninety degrees.

scenes.caption: Obtuse: 120°
scenes.say: At four o'clock the hands open wider. That is an obtuse angle, one hundred and twenty degrees.

scenes.caption: Straight line: 180°
scenes.say: At six o'clock the hands make a straight line. That is one hundred and eighty degrees.

blocks.alt: Three triangles labelled acute, right and obtuse with their angle sizes
blocks.caption: Acute, right and obtuse triangles.
blocks.say: An acute angle is smaller than ninety degrees. A right angle is ninety. An obtuse angle is bigger.

blocks.markdown:
A **polygon** has straight sides. 3 triangle, 4 quadrilateral, 5 pentagon, 6 hexagon, 8 octagon.

A square is a special rectangle with four equal sides.
blocks.say: A polygon is a flat shape with straight sides. We name polygons by how many sides they have. Three sides make a triangle. Four make a quadrilateral. Five make a pentagon. Six make a hexagon. Eight make an octagon. A square is a special quadrilateral: it has four equal sides and four right angles. A rectangle has four right angles and opposite sides equal. So every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.

blocks.markdown:
A shape is **symmetrical** if one half matches the other. The fold is the **line of symmetry**.

A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle has 2.
blocks.say: A shape is symmetrical if you can fold it in half and both sides match exactly. The fold line is called the line of symmetry, or mirror line. Look at the butterfly. Fold it down the middle, and the two wings match. A square has four lines of symmetry. A rectangle that is not a square has two.

scenes.caption: Both halves match
scenes.say: Fold along the line and the left wing sits exactly on the right wing. They match, so the butterfly is symmetrical.

blocks.markdown:
Islamic star patterns use **repeating** shapes with many lines of symmetry.

An eight-pointed star has 8 lines of symmetry.
blocks.say: Many mosques have beautiful tile patterns made from symmetrical stars. These patterns are built from simple shapes, like squares, triangles and hexagons, repeated again and again. They have many lines of symmetry. An eight-pointed star has eight lines of symmetry. Artists planned them with only a ruler and compass.

blocks.markdown:
**Coordinates** give a position: (3, 2) means 3 across and 2 up.

Across first, then up.
blocks.say: Coordinates tell us exactly where a point is on a grid. Two numbers in brackets. The first number says how far across, the second says how far up. Think of it as along the corridor, then up the stairs. The point three, two is three across and two up. Always across first, then up.

scenes.say: Start at zero, zero in the bottom left corner. The numbers along the bottom count across. The numbers up the side count up.

scenes.caption: then 2 up: (3, 2)
scenes.say: Then two squares up. We are at three, two.

question.prompt: Which point is 4 across and 1 up?

blocks.markdown: A **reflection** is a mirror image. Each point is the same distance from the mirror line, on the other side.
blocks.say: When we reflect a shape, every point is the same distance from the mirror line. The point sits on the other side. If the mirror is vertical, a point two squares left ends up two squares right. The shape is the same size, just flipped.

scenes.caption: 2 left of the mirror
scenes.say: A star is two squares to the left of the mirror line.

scenes.caption: 2 right of the mirror
scenes.say: Its reflection is two squares to the right. Same distance, other side.

question.explanation: A reflection is the same distance on the opposite side.

question.prompt: The point (2, 5) is 2 across and 5 up.

blocks.say: Remember. Coordinates are across first, then up. A reflection is the same distance on the other side of the mirror.

blocks.markdown:
**Faces** are flat surfaces, **edges** are where faces meet, and **vertices** are corners.

A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
blocks.say: 3D shapes have faces, edges and vertices. A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner. A cube has six faces, twelve edges and eight vertices. Many buildings use 3D shapes. A minaret is a cylinder. A mosque dome is a half sphere. A pyramid has a square base.

question.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?

blocks.markdown: A **net** is a flat shape that folds into a 3D shape. A cube's net has 6 squares.
blocks.say: A net is a flat pattern that folds up into a 3D shape. The net of a cube is six squares joined together. If you cut a cardboard box along its edges and flatten it, you get a net. Watch six squares fold up into a cube.

scenes.caption: A net of 6 squares
scenes.say: Six squares joined in a cross shape. This is a net.

scenes.caption: Folding up
scenes.say: Fold the sides up. The squares start to make a box.

scenes.caption: A cube
scenes.say: And it is a cube! Six faces, twelve edges and eight vertices.
